data.claim: Resumption is safe only if the system implements an atomic checkpoint that consistently pairs a full state snapshot with the last committed event's identity (hash and sequence number). The checkpoint and the log must be updated in a single atomic transaction. Resumption is safe when the checkpoint's recorded event identity exactly matches the actual log tail. Resumption must be refused when the checkpoint is stale (behind the log tail—some committed events are not in the snapshot), when the checkpoint is ahead (the snapshot references events not yet durable in the log), or when no checkpoint exists at all.
